vagueSymptom: Every week someone phones the front desk to ask what our refund window is. Several have told us they had the season pass page open on the rules-and-refunds panel while they were asking, and still could not tell us what it said.
plantedCondition: manifest.palette.textMuted is #6e737c instead of #4a4f57. The token passes AA on the page's white surfaces (4.77:1) and fails on the recessed rules-and-refunds panel surface #d2d6da (3.26:1), where the refund-window sentence lives. Four further defects — X-Robots-Tag: noindex on the document, a missing alt attribute on the pass-comparison graphic, a console.error-reported TypeError in the closures-notice renderer, and an h2→h4 skip in the sign-up section — are unconditional fixture furniture present under both manifests and explain nothing.

requiredDiagnosisFacts.fact: Body text in the rules-and-refunds panel renders at roughly 3.3:1 against the panel background, below the 4.5:1 contrast requirement for normal text.
requiredDiagnosisFacts.why: This is the condition itself, stated as a measured fact rather than as a category.

requiredDiagnosisFacts.fact: The refund-window sentence is one of the affected nodes.
requiredDiagnosisFacts.why: Ties the condition to the artifact the symptom names; a generic 'the page has contrast problems' does not select.

requiredDiagnosisFacts.fact: The same muted text colour passes on the page's white surfaces; the failure is specific to the composition with the recessed panel surface.
requiredDiagnosisFacts.why: Distinguishes a real diagnosis from 'the page's grey text is too light', and is the fact that proves the agent read node-level attribution rather than a category score.

requiredDiagnosisFacts.fact: This is why a caller with the page open cannot read the refund window.
requiredDiagnosisFacts.why: The oracle grades interpretation; the causal link must be stated, not implied.

requiredEvidence.evidence: The report establishes the state of the page across more than one audit category, naming the other defective conditions it found.
requiredEvidence.why: Breadth is what the case exists to price. A report that names only one condition has not shown it knows the condition is the culprit.

requiredEvidence.evidence: A contrast ratio for the refund sentence (or the panel body text containing it) and the threshold it fails, from a capture command with a transcript ordinal.
requiredEvidence.why: The load-bearing measurement. A qualitative 'the text is too light' is not established.

requiredEvidence.evidence: Each of the noindex directive, the missing alt attribute on the pass-comparison graphic, the console-reported TypeError and missing closures banner, and the skipped heading level is named and excluded with a reason tied to an observation.
requiredEvidence.why: This is the selection property. Naming the right answer without excluding the alternatives does not distinguish a diagnosis from a guess.

requiredEvidence.evidence: The refund sentence is present at full size in the rendered DOM.
requiredEvidence.why: Rules out the console-error story specifically, which is the most causal-looking competitor.

plausibleWrongAnswer: The document response carries X-Robots-Tag: noindex, so the page is excluded from search and people cannot find it. (A real planted condition — the cheapest single observation on the fixture — that explains nothing about a caller who already has the page open.)

environment.chromeBuild: Chrome for Testing 143.0.7499.40 (full build; NOT chrome-headless-shell)
